---
title: "Seasonal stage x Bd modeling"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: per-species Bayesian models of how the subadult - adult difference in *Bd* infection
changes through the season (stage x season), following the glmmTMB screen in
`01_season_screen.Rmd`.

Design decisions (see the screen and brainstorm):

- **No weather terms.** Within temperate species, 30-day temperature is largely seasonal, so
  stage x season and stage x temperature cannot be separated. The seasonal curves here therefore
  include whatever climate comes with the season. The unified model keeps weather for its own
  purpose (adjusting the overall subadult - adult contrast).
- **One model per species**, for the species with enough co-sampling of both life stages:
  *A. canorus* and five ranids. The two-window Panamanian species (*Colostethus*,
  *L. warszewitschii*) are dropped: their life stages are mostly sampled in different windows.
- **Same random-effect structure as the GAM models**, so differences from them come from the
  seasonal terms, not the random effects.

Production fits run on the cluster with `r-brms-contained/size_bd_season_modeling.R` (same data
prep, formula, priors and settings; `hpc/run_size_bd_season_modeling.sbatch` fits each species as
an array task). Keep the two in sync.

Run order: needs the unified model data from `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd` (the same file
model m11g was fit to).

# Setup

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr)

models_dir = here("size_bd_season", "models")
dir.create(models_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

```

# Data
```{r}
# species with enough co-sampled weeks of both life stages (screen tier 1, 10 / 6), minus the
# two-window panamanian species. alphabetical order = cluster array index (0-5)
season_species = c("anaxyrus_canorus",
                   "rana_cascadae",
                   "rana_catesbeiana",
                   "rana_clamitans",
                   "rana_muscosa",
                   "rana_sierrae")

# season covariate: months from july 1 (day 182). centering and scaling only changes the units
# of the smooth's linear (unpenalized) part, which makes its prior easier to set: a slope of 1
# means a change of 1 on the logit (hu) or log (mu) scale per month.
prep_season_data = function(brms_data, species_name) {
  brms_data %>%
    filter(taxon_capture == species_name) %>%
    mutate(life_stage_simple = factor(life_stage_simple, levels = c("adult", "subadult")),
           doy = as.integer(format(date, "%j")),
           season_m = (doy - 182) / 30.44) %>%
    # drop unused levels so random-effect terms have no empty columns
    droplevels()
}

season_data = purrr::map(set_names(season_species), ~ prep_season_data(brms_data, .x))

# sample sizes per species and stage
map_dfr(season_data, ~ count(.x, life_stage_simple), .id = "taxon_capture") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = life_stage_simple, values_from = n)

```

# Model structure
```{r}

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

# for both the load part (mu, log scale, Bd-positive swabs) and the detection part (hu, logit
# scale of non-detection):
#   1 + life_stage_simple            stage intercepts (adult reference)
#   s(season_m, by = life_stage_simple, k = 5)
#                                    a separate seasonal curve per stage. a thin-plate spline,
#                                    not cyclic: most species cover only part of the year, so the
#                                    curve is a within-season shape, not a full annual cycle.
#                                    k = 5 allows one dip-and-recovery (e.g. r. cascadae) without
#                                    much wiggle. the subadult - adult contrast at a date is the
#                                    gap between the two curves.
#   (1 | population:life_stage_simple)
#                                    population effects, separate by stage (as in unified / gam)
#   (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year)
#                                    population-year effects, correlated between stages
# sigma ~ 1 + (1 | population)       residual spread of log load varies by population (as in gam)
season_formula = bf(
  bd_load_co100_density ~ 1 + life_stage_simple +
    s(season_m, by = life_stage_simple, k = 5) +
    (1 | population:life_stage_simple) +
    (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year),

  hu ~ 1 + life_stage_simple +
    s(season_m, by = life_stage_simple, k = 5) +
    (1 | population:life_stage_simple) +
    (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year),

  sigma ~ 1 + (1 | population)
)

# priors, on the same scales as the unified model (m11g). classes:
#   Intercept:  intercept (adult, at the centered predictors)
#   b:          the subadult offset AND the linear (unpenalized) part of each seasonal smooth
#               (coef "sseason_m:life_stage_simple<stage>_1", per month). the class-wide b prior
#               covers the subadult offset; the smooths' linear parts get their own prior by coef
#   sds:        how wiggly each smooth may be. the brms default here is student_t(3, 0, 6)
#               (scaled from the data), which allows very wiggly curves, especially on the logit
#               (hu) scale; student_t(3, 0, 2.5) is moderately regularizing but still allows
#               rises of several log units (e.g. r. sierrae subadult load)
#   sd:         random-effect sds
season_priors = c(
  # mu: log load density among positives
  prior(normal(5, 4), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 3), class = "b"),                                              # subadult offset
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simpleadult_1"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simplesubadult_1"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sds"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),

  # hu: logit of non-detection
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", dpar = "hu"),                                 # subadult offset
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simpleadult_1", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simplesubadult_1", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sds", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "hu"),

  # sigma: log residual sd of log load
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept", dpar = "sigma"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "sigma")
)

# validate_prior errors if any prior does not match a model parameter, and shows the full prior
# set (ours, plus brms defaults for anything not set, e.g. the lkj(1) prior on the adult /
# subadult population-year correlation). the coef names come from the stage levels, so they are
# the same for every species; checking one species is enough.
validate_prior(season_priors,
               formula = season_formula,
               data = season_data[["anaxyrus_canorus"]],
               family = hurdle_lognormal())

```

# Local timing test
```{r}
#| eval: false

# short run of the real model, to estimate cluster run time and memory. warmup = 300 clears
# stan's adaptation threshold (below ~150-200 warmup the adaptation schedule is compressed and
# timing is not representative, see r-brms-contained/hpc/timing_probe.sbatch).
#
# extrapolating: sampling time scales roughly linearly with post-warmup iterations, warmup less
# predictably (step size adapts). the estimate below scales the slowest chain's warmup by
# 2000 / 300 and its sampling by 2000 / 100 (production: 2000 warmup + 2000 sampling; chains run
# in parallel, so the slowest chain sets the wall time). treat it as an order of magnitude, and
# compare species to see how time grows with n.
timing_species = c("anaxyrus_canorus", "rana_cascadae", "rana_sierrae")   # n ~1k and ~3.4k; add rana_sierrae (~26.5k) if time allows

timing_results = map_dfr(timing_species, function(spp) {
  start = Sys.time()
  fit = brm(
    formula = season_formula,
    data = season_data[[spp]],
    family = hurdle_lognormal(),
    prior = season_priors,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
    chains = 4, iter = 400, warmup = 300,
    seed = 127, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
    refresh = 0
  )
  elapsed = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "mins"))

  # per-chain warmup / sampling seconds from stan (excludes compilation)
  chain_times = rstan::get_elapsed_time(fit$fit)

  tibble(taxon_capture = spp,
         n = nrow(season_data[[spp]]),
         total_min = elapsed,                                 # includes compilation (~1 min)
         max_chain_warmup_s = max(chain_times[, "warmup"]),
         max_chain_sample_s = max(chain_times[, "sample"]),
         # production estimate: warmup scaled 2000/300, sampling scaled 2000/100
         est_production_h = (max(chain_times[, "warmup"]) * 2000 / 300 +
                               max(chain_times[, "sample"]) * 2000 / 100) / 3600,
         divergences = sum(nuts_params(fit) %>% filter(Parameter == "divergent__") %>% pull(Value)))
})

timing_results

```

# Model fitting
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show model fitting code"

# production fits run on the cluster (r-brms-contained/hpc/run_size_bd_season_modeling.sbatch).
# this local version is for reference or a single small species.
fit_season_model = function(spp) {
  fit = brm(
    formula = season_formula,
    data = season_data[[spp]],
    family = hurdle_lognormal(),
    prior = season_priors,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
    chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000,
    seed = 127, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr"
  )

  fit = add_criterion(fit, "loo")
  saveRDS(fit, file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_season_model_zln_s1_", spp, ".rds")))
  fit
}

# e.g. fit_season_model("anaxyrus_canorus")

```

# Load fitted models
```{r}
#| eval: false

# cluster fits are copied into size_bd_season/models/ (named as in fit_season_model)
season_models = map(set_names(season_species), function(spp) {
  readRDS(file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_season_model_zln_s1_", spp, ".rds")))
})

```
